prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling reactions

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B004 with Buchwald and Hartwig. After round 1 the case rests on the criterion the chair asked about, that reproducibility and clean attribution should count when no ballot has a majority. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling has about thirty years of independent confirmation, a defined mechanism (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination from amido complexes), ligand generations developed in parallel by two groups, and a two-name credit that matches the record. Its use is visible in medicinal-chemistry and process routes and in materials, so the consequences are in the literature and not in projections. Nobody in round 1 disputed the quality of the chemistry or the attribution; the objections were closeness to the 2010 prize and, from me, the Kosugi precursor. The first is a framing question, because the bond class and the rate-limiting step differ from C-C coupling, and the second can be handled in the citation and the background text without adding a third name. A citation limited to general catalytic C-N coupling avoids claiming more than the two groups established.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still the proximity to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. I think the distinct bond class and mechanistic bottleneck answer it, but I cannot show that the whole committee will accept this, and a decision to avoid a second palladium prize within sixteen years would be legitimate. Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling is an earlier priority claim that I regard as a non-general, non-catalytic-in-amine precursor, but I have still not verified the priority record, and expert reports should check it. The field also has less breadth of public interest than the biology-facing ballots, which is a presentation issue and not a scientific one. I have no counted survey of adoption, so my statements about its prevalence are from memory of the literature.

responses.point: Chabes holds B068 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and says that if the glue lineage is to be covered, Handa should replace Ciulli, to be tested in round 2.
responses.response: That test is what makes me hesitate. A prize that cites designed induced proximity (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) leaves out the cereblon lineage that you yourself say has the stronger link to approved drugs, and a prize that includes Handa changes the citation from a chemical design principle to a mix of a target-identification result and a design concept. I find the concept real and kept B068 as my first alternative, but I do not see a three-name citation without a visible hole, and no PROTAC is approved. If the committee does choose B068, I would back a citation narrowly about PROTACs and structure-guided ternary-complex design, which is Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and say plainly in the text that the glue lineage is a separate discovery. I do not think that settles the issue for a first-choice vote.

responses.point: Linke asks whether a B003 citation can be written for liquid-liquid demixing and multivalency without asserting that particular condensates are phase-separated in vivo, and whether Rosen is still the third name.
responses.response: As the synthetic chemist on the committee I cannot judge the in vivo evidence, so I rely on the disagreement among those who can: Sparr and you say the core is secure, while Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou say the biological claims are not. A citation limited to the physical principle is possible, and it would be more defensible than a claim about cellular organisation, but then the molecular-level credit goes to the people who gave that principle quantitative form. That is the place where Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag becomes a hard allocation, and I see no way to settle it from the credit list. This is why I weigh B003 below B004: the principle may be right, but the citation and the third name both still need to be argued, while for B004 they do not.

responses.point: Brzezinski favours nitrogenase (B009) with Rees, Dean and Seefeldt, with a citation worded around structure and cofactor chemistry, and says that his preference partly reflects his own interest.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure, and I agree that B009 is mature and that a structure-and-cofactor citation is the right wording. My difficulty is the allocation: you and Zou disagree on whether Dean or Einsle should be third, Ribbe is in neither trio, and the unresolved N2 reduction mechanism means the citation has to stop short of what the title of the discovery implies. That is the same sort of attribution problem I am asked to accept for B003 and B068. B004 has none of these, and I think that when no ballot has a majority a candidate with a clean pair should be a real fallback for those who value maturity. I would not oppose B009 if the credit is settled, but the third name remains unresolved for me.

responses.point: Aqvist holds base editing (B024) first with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, valuing a conceptually simple tool, and in round 1 I questioned what was new chemically.
responses.response: Your reply that a deaminase evolved to act on DNA is real chemistry and protein engineering is fair, and I accept that the clinical record in individual patients is more advanced than for PROTACs. I still read the central advance as an engineered protein fusion built on the 2020 recognition, with Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID priority open, and you list the same reservations yourself, including that prime editing may later be the more general advance. I did not change my view, but your argument has moved base editing from a case I would exclude to one I would reconsider in a later year, especially if the committee later considers it together with prime editing.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 prize, or accept a distinct bond class and mechanistic bottleneck as a separate achievement
Whether the Kosugi 1983 priority record, which I have not verified, changes the credit in any way beyond a statement in the citation text
Whether, if no ballot reaches a majority, members will treat a clean two-name, mature candidate as an acceptable fallback instead of waiting for a conceptually broader prize
How widely the method is used in pharmaceutical routes, which I cite from memory and not from a counted survey
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B004 or for any of my alternatives: I have no recorded tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or the B068 and B023 candidates. My mentor Masamune and my institutional ties (Chalmers, KTH, Lund, Tartu) do not intersect with any shortlisted candidate that I can identify. I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr, which bears on no candidate. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
